title: Fast Linear Solvers via AI-Tuned Markov Chain Monte Carlo-based Matrix Inversion
problem: Solving large sparse linear systems is pervasive in science/engineering; Krylov solvers can be slow for ill-conditioned matrices; MCMC-based preconditioners effective but parameter selection is manual/grid-search (costly)
motivation: Automate MCMC parameter selection using AI; reduce search cost and convergence iterations through intelligent parameter tuning
method: AI-driven framework using graph neural network surrogate to predict preconditioning speed; Bayesian acquisition function selects parameter sets minimizing iterations; applied to ill-conditioned linear systems
key_novelty: Graph neural surrogate for MCMC parameter prediction; Bayesian optimization of preconditioner parameters; integration with Krylov solvers
contributions: Graph neural surrogate predicting MCMC preconditioning performance
Bayesian acquisition function for parameter optimization
50% reduction in search budget compared to conventional methods
10% reduction in convergence iterations on test systems
Practical framework for large-scale linear system solving
limitations: Abstract does not specify which Krylov method used; scalability to extremely ill-conditioned systems unclear; comparison with other surrogate models limited
